definition: A nuclear reaction in which two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy because the product is more tightly bound; it needs a very high temperature and density, as in the core of a star.
The long, stable stage of a star's life in which it fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, with the outward force from radiation and gas pressure balancing the inward gravitational force.
A large, luminous star with a cool, red surface that has used up the hydrogen in its core and now fuses hydrogen in a shell around the core, or helium in the core.
The small, very dense, hot core left when a star of up to about 8 solar masses sheds its outer layers; no fusion happens in it, so it slowly cools.
